chapter: Jamming, bootleg records and the Topsy hit
title: Bootleg recordings of jam sessions and concerts
summary: Tapes of jam sessions and concerts get sold abroad; Cole recalls a manager ripping out hidden wires.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: That's right, that's right, and no paid admission. But to go out there and sit in and jam where people are paying to come in that door, all they giving you is just a drink and a sandwich or a steak, whatever, you know, you got money, you can buy that. So you know and so those things I wouldn't think of doing again, you know. Like a lot of times, oh used to jam downtown, Hawkins, all of us, Billy Butterfield, all of us, both white and black, go down there and jam, and in the back room they would have their little turntable on ... with those tapes, and be picking up on everything that you do. Now of course while you're there, you see, they would have all the whiskey you wanted to drink and good food, chicks around, you know, and it was a glamorous setting. Man, the first thing you knew, you go over in Europe, about five months later and you'd hear all this on the air. What the hell is that? When did I make that? And that's your

record that you was down there jamming and they was back there getting it off the tape, making a master of it, going over there in Europe and selling them to those different companies. There you are playing.
And you didn't get a dime for it?

No, no you don't get no money for that. That's the same way with everything, you've got to be so careful. Like drums, they have good makes of drums, good [chicks] on drums, different drums over there that are very good. They may bring them to a concert where you're playing and want you to look at them, you know. And if you don't know, see you walk over to the set and get behind the set, And say ooh, this is beautiful, this is nice and bang, they'll take a picture of that and as soon as you leave town....
Cozy Cole endorses such and such drums.

That's right, and you don't know anything about it. Till somebody tells you about it, and then they start passing the buck, oh no, I didn't do this, and then it's too late then, they've got it out, they maybe sold some drums behind that. I'll never forget a place where we did play with Louie, had a manager by the name of Pierre Tallery, a Frenchman. And they had this makeshift bandstand was outside and Frenchy hollered back to Louie, 'don't start until I tell ya,' So we was walking along around in front of the bandstand, it was just about to get dark, and he was kicking out wires from underneath the bandstand, looked up

in the trees, son of a guns up there sitting with their little tapes and things going, and they were going to tape the whole concert if he didn't know it. He tore down all that and then we went on and started playing. Oh yeah. You've got to really know what's going on in order to, you know ....
Oh no, and what're you going to do about it? You can't do anything about it. You're over here and they're over there.
The only thing you can do is invest money in a lawyer and it's not worth the trouble.
No, no because you may end up with nothing.
Or more in legal fees then you get back.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. So you've got to be very very careful. And I imagine there isn't too much of that going on now, you know, too many musicians are hep to what's going on.
There's still quite a lot of bootlegging going on.
Of things that go all the way back to the 20s and '30s.
